stem: A unit implements a new fall-prevention intervention as part of a quality-improvement project. Which action best evaluates whether the intervention improved care?

options.A: Compare relevant client outcomes before and after the intervention
options.B: Assume the intervention is effective because staff completed the required education
options.C: Continue the intervention indefinitely without reviewing outcome data
options.D: Evaluate only whether the intervention increased the amount of documentation completed

rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places performance improvement within Management of Care and specifically includes evaluating the impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use. Comparing relevant outcomes before and after an intervention directly evaluates its effect on care. Staff education completion, continued implementation without outcome review, or documentation volume alone does not establish that client outcomes improved.
educational_objective: Evaluate a quality-improvement intervention by comparing relevant client-care outcomes after implementation with appropriate baseline data.
source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_locator: Detailed Test Plan, Management of Care → Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22 / PDF p.26: participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes; evaluate the impact of performance improvement measures on client care and resource use
source_claim_supported: Entry-level RNs participate in quality-improvement processes and evaluate the impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use.

correction_summary: Replaced the source item's Magnet redesignation-cycle trivia with an NCLEX-relevant quality-improvement application item. Although current ANCC materials support a four-year Magnet designation/redesignation cycle, memorizing that credentialing interval does not directly test an entry-level RN activity statement. The revised item directly tests the NCSBN 2026 requirement to evaluate the impact of performance-improvement measures on client care.
audit_findings: A directly operationalizes the NCSBN activity statement by evaluating client outcomes. B confuses process completion with effectiveness; C omits evaluation; D measures documentation volume rather than the impact on client care. No second answer, cueing, unsupported numeric precision, or weak blueprint fit remains. The construct is materially more NCLEX-relevant than the original Magnet-cycle recall item.
